scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: A Kindle screen looks like real paper, and its battery lasts for weeks. How is it so different from a phone?

scenes.name: capsules
scenes.text: E-ink screens are packed with millions of tiny capsules, about as wide as a human hair.

scenes.name: particles
scenes.text: Each capsule holds white particles with a negative charge, and black particles with a positive charge, floating in clear fluid.

scenes.name: move
scenes.text: Electrodes under each spot pull one colour up to the top. That's what you see as a dot of black or white.

scenes.name: power
scenes.text: Once the particles move, they stay put without power. Energy is only used when the page changes.

scenes.name: light
scenes.text: It doesn't shine light at your eyes. It reflects room light like paper, so it's easy to read in sunlight.

scenes.name: slow
scenes.text: Moving particles is slow, so e-ink flashes when refreshing, and it's not good for video.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Charged ink, moved by electricity, holds still for free. Follow for more on how things really work.
